2026-12-01.title: Tuesday of the First Week of Advent
readings: The Spirit of the Lord shall rest on him
Justice shall flourish in his time, and fullness of peace for ever
Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit
2026-12-01.verse: Blessed are the eyes that see what you see! For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but did not see it.
theo: Isaiah sees a shoot coming out of the stump of Jesse, the cut-down family tree of David. On this shoot the Spirit of the Lord rests: wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge and fear of the Lord. These are the gifts the Church sees fulfilled in Christ and shared with us in Confirmation (CCC 1831). Under his rule the wolf lives with the lamb and “the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD”.

In the Gospel Jesus, “rejoicing in the Holy Spirit”, thanks the Father for revealing these things not to the wise and intelligent but to “infants”. Then he tells his disciples that they see what prophets and kings longed to see. Advent invites us to become little enough to receive, and to recognise how blessed we are to know Christ.
outline: Ask: what new life can God bring from a cut-down stump in your life?
Point 1 · A shoot from the stump
God begins again from what seems dead.
Point 2 · The Spirit rests on him
The seven gifts of the Messiah, shared with us.
Blessed are the eyes that see.
“Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.”
live: Each day this week pray for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
Ask a child a question about God and listen to the answer.
2026-12-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, shoot from the stump of Jesse, let your Spirit rest on me too. Make me little enough to receive what you reveal, and grateful to see what prophets and kings longed to see. Amen.
altar: At this Mass the Holy Spirit who rested on the shoot of Jesse comes down upon the gifts. The little ones to whom the Father reveals his secrets are fed with the Body of his Son.

quick: God brings new life from a cut-down stump.
The Spirit of the Lord rests on the Messiah.
God reveals himself to the little ones.
2026-12-01.action: Pray each day for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
2026-12-01.question: Am I too “wise” to receive what God reveals to the little ones?

family.explain: Isaiah saw a new branch growing from an old stump, and animals living in peace. Jesus brings new life and peace, and a little child leads them.
family.intention: We pray for peace in our home and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Where do we need God's peace in our family this Advent?”

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, who rested on the shoot of Jesse. As we begin Advent, fill us with your gifts and make us little children before the Father. Amen.
share: Isaiah speaks of a shoot from a stump (Isaiah 11:1). What in my life looks finished, and could God bring it back to life?
Jesus says the Father reveals his secrets to infants (Luke 10:21). Where do I need to become little again?
Which gift of the Holy Spirit do I most need this Advent?
pm.resp: Come, Lord Jesus, Prince of Peace.
interc: For the Church, that she may be renewed by the Holy Spirit this Advent.
For places of war and hatred, that the peace of Isaiah's vision may come.
For those who feel their life is finished, that God may make new shoots spring up.
For children, that they may lead us to simplicity and trust.
For our group, that we may grow in the gifts of the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your Son to the little ones. Make us humble and open, fill us with the Spirit of wisdom and peace, and prepare us to welcome Jesus at Christmas. Amen.

illus: After a cyclone flattened a coconut grove near Alappuzha, the farmer thought everything was lost. Weeks later he noticed green shoots rising from the stumps of trees he had given up for dead. He said: “God showed me Advent in my own field.”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this first weekday of Advent Isaiah shows us a stump. The great family tree of David has been cut down; it looks dead. Yet the prophet says: a shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots (Isaiah 11:1). Advent begins with hope where everything seems finished.

Upon this shoot the Spirit of the Lord will rest: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and might, of knowledge and the fear of the Lord (Isaiah 11:2). The Church sees here the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, which Christ possesses in fullness and shares with us in Confirmation.

And the fruit of this King is peace: the wolf shall live with the lamb, the leopard lie down with the kid, and a little child shall lead them (Isaiah 11:6). It is a picture of creation healed. Old enemies are reconciled. The violence of the strong gives way to the trust of the small.

In the Gospel Jesus rejoices in the Holy Spirit and thanks the Father, because these things have been hidden from the wise and the intelligent and revealed to infants (Luke 10:21). God's secrets are opened not to the proud but to the little ones.

Advent asks us to become little again: to admit our need, to stop pretending to have everything under control, to receive like children. The little child of Isaiah's prophecy leads the wild animals; the little Child of Bethlehem will lead us to peace.

Is there a stump in your life, something that looks finished: a marriage, a vocation, a friendship, your prayer? Bring it to the Lord this Advent. He can make a shoot spring from it. And ask the Holy Spirit to renew his seven gifts in you, so that you may be ready for Christmas. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus was happy when little ones understood God. God loves to show His secrets to children. Thank Him today in a short prayer!

intro: God starts again from what seems dead; his Spirit rests on the Messiah; the little ones see.

sub: David's family tree was cut down.
God begins again where we see an end.
q: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.

At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants; yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.”
points.apply: Bring one “dead stump” in your life to God in prayer.

q: The wolf shall live with the lamb, the leopard shall lie down with the kid, the calf and the lion and the fatling together.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
points.apply: Make peace with one person this Advent.

points.h: Blessed are the eyes that see
sub: Prophets and kings longed to see.
We see Christ in Word and Sacrament.
q: Many peoples shall come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths.”

Then turning to the disciples, Jesus said to them privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see! For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.”
points.apply: Thank God tonight for the gift of faith.

concl: God's new beginnings come from small shoots.
Become little, and you will see.
2026-12-01.resolve: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each morning this Advent.
